answer: Like a lotus that only opens when its roots have sunk deep, an agent economy can resist sybils with stake-linked reputation vines: every identity must lock a small refundable bond that grows with each verified transaction, so trust spreads like a vine through real history. A lantern of public attestation then lights each agent's past — new identities start dim, and a single operator spinning up thousands of sock puppets must fund every bond and every fake history, turning cheap duplication into a cost that scales faster than the reward.
